question.text: The magnetic field vector of an electromagnetic wave is given by <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>B</mi><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>B</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mfrac><mrow><mover><mi mathvariant="normal">i</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mo>+</mo><mover><mi mathvariant="normal">j</mi><mo>^</mo></mover></mrow><msqrt><mn>2</mn></msqrt></mfrac><mi>cos</mi><mfenced><mrow><mi>k</mi><mi>z</mi><mo>-</mo><mi>ω</mi><mi>t</mi></mrow></mfenced></math> where <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mover><mi mathvariant="normal">i</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mo>,</mo><mo> </mo><mover><mi mathvariant="normal">j</mi><mo>^</mo></mover></math> represents unit vector along <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>x</mi></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>y</mi></math>-axis respectively. At <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mo>,</mo></math> two electric charges <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>q</mi><mn>1</mn></msub></math> of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>4</mn><mi>π</mi></math> coulomb and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>q</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></math> of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>2</mn><mi>π</mi></math> coulomb located at <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfenced><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mo> </mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mo> </mo><mfrac><mi>π</mi><mi>k</mi></mfrac></mrow></mfenced></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfenced><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mo> </mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mo> </mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>3</mn><mi>π</mi></mrow><mi>k</mi></mfrac></mrow></mfenced><mo>,</mo></math> respectively, have the same velocity of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>0</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>5</mn><mi mathvariant="normal">c</mi><mover><mi mathvariant="normal">i</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mo>,</mo></math> (where <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>c</mi></math> is the velocity of light ). The ratio of the force acting on charge <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>q</mi><mn>1</mn></msub></math> to <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>q</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></math> is :
